text:
Maria: Quick post-mortem note — this morning a high-priority Dedicated tenant (acme-prod) hit an allocation eviction and we routed ~120 reqs/min to hosted fallback for ~7m. Observability shows increased tail latency for that tenant during the window.
Alex: Ugh. Did dedicated honor their QoS isolation predicate?
Maria: It did for CPU/GPU, but we exceeded pool burst capacity and our spillover policy kicked in (region -> hosted) instead of queueing.
Kevin: Can we confirm whether this was a policy decision or config drift? I remember changing default spillover from "queue" to "fallback" in feb rollout.
Sarah: That change was intentional to avoid tail latency for other Dedicated tenants — if one tenant heaps requests, we wanted them to fail fast to protect others. But for high-tier customers we might want a different behavior.
Alex: The real debate: should the platform expose spillover as an API signal (a field on response: `fallback_reason`) or keep it console-only? Ops teams want programmatic hooks.
Maria: Ops asked to suppress data-plane exposure for security/cost reasons. Billing doesn't want customers programmatically seeing we used hosted capacity since it changes metering.
Kevin: Billing aside, telemetry folks want a per-tenant tag on traces: `route_variant: hosted/fallback/dedicated` so we can build dashboards. We can redact exact capacity metrics if needed.
Sarah: UX also raised a concern — product customers see confusing "fallback" badges in console if we show every spillover event. Need aggregation and retention policy.
Alex: Proposal: three-pronged approach:
1) Data-plane: return lightweight header `X-Route-Variant: hosted|dedicated` for internal customers only (flagged by tenant tier). No public SDK change.
2) Control-plane: emit event `route.fallback` to event bus with anonymized capacity_id + tenant_hash for billing/legal.
3) Console: show aggregated spillover counts per day + clickable timeline with redacted raw logs.
Kevin: That sounds reasonable. One open thing: model-variant fallback vs region fallback. This incident chose region->hosted; we could have used model-variant fallback (serve quantized variant on same pool) which would have kept tenant in Dedicated but potentially lower quality.
Maria: Right — for acme-prod they opted into "no-quality-regressions" SLA, so model-variant fallback was disabled in their policy. The tenant policy should be honored.
Sarah: UX question: should we allow tenants to set a precedence order in console: e.g., prefer `model_variant` over `region_fallback` or always respect tenant SLA?
Alex: I'd prefer precedence configurable at the tenant level, with sensible defaults per tier. Free/default = region fallback, Enterprise = model-variant first if allowed.
Kevin: Telemetry change needed: we must tag which fallback path was chosen (`fallback_path: variant|region|none`) and capture metrics: spilled_reqs, avg_latency_delta, cost_delta. These can be emitted as metrics to datadog.
Maria: Billing needs cost_delta per fallback minute to reconcile hosted usage. We need a deterministic calculation: hosted_tokens_billed - tokens_that_would_have_been_billed_on_dedicated (approx).
Sarah: Also, rollout UX: when we change default policy we must surface a changelog + allow per-tenant overrides. We broke a few expectations when feb change landed.
Alex: Internal API debate: exposing `X-Route-Variant` breaks ideal of single unified API semantics. But internal customers (partners) need it. Can we gate via a tenant capability flag `expose_route_variant`?
Kevin: Yes. Add capability gating to the tenant profile. Default off. Turn on for internal partners only.
Maria: Ops-bot: we should also emit an incident-like short alert when spillover > threshold (e.g., >50rps for 5m) so SRE can review.
ops-bot: alert created: spillover-high-acme-prod (id: se-1842), severity: low, trigger: 120rps for 7m, runbook: /runbooks/spillover.md
Sarah: Action items:
- Kevin: add `fallback_path` + `route_variant` telemetry fields and a datadog metric (spilled_reqs, cost_delta).
- Alex: add tenant capability `expose_route_variant` and implement `X-Route-Variant` header gated by it.
- Maria: iterate console mockups for aggregated spillover timeline + per-tenant policy precedence UI.
- Ops: adjust alert thresholds and add runbook link to notifications.
Kevin: I'll open an RFC for telemetry schema and propose metric names.
Alex: I'll prototype header gating in internal API proxy and add tests for hiding header for public tenants.
Maria: We should also add a short privacy/legal note: never expose exact capacity ids in API or logs; use hashes.
Sarah: Agreed. Let's reconvene after RFC + mockups. @deploy-bot can you schedule a canary for the header prototype behind a feature flag?
deploy-bot: scheduled canary: header-gate-v1 on infra-canary-3, window: 60m, owners: Alex, Kevin
Alex: Thanks. If no objections, I'll start the implementation today and aim for staging by EOD.
Kevin: No objections from me.
Maria: Thanks all — good discussion. We'll track progress in the RFC and link here. :white_check_mark:
